place.pt: Atlantic Europe and the Western Mediterranean

stages.name: Local peoples
stages.desc: Independent peoples and kingdoms outside the tin route's control

stages.name: Independent tin lands
stages.desc: Tin-producing regions worked and traded by their own peoples

stages.name: Greek routes
stages.desc: Lands crossed by the Greek tin trade of Massalia

stages.name: Punic ports
stages.desc: Coasts held by Carthage and the Phoenician cities of the west

stages.name: Reached by Rome
stages.desc: Under Roman rule or within Rome's reach

states.name: France
timeline: Massalia's merchants buy tin carried overland through Gaul from the Atlantic
Pytheas of Massalia sails north to Britain
Rome conquers southern Gaul, the province of Transalpine Gaul
The Roman colony of Narbo is founded on the road to Spain

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Phoenician Lixus and the trading post of Mogador on the Atlantic coast
Carthage's fall leaves the Punic towns of the coast to the kings of Mauretania

states.name: Spain
timeline: Gadir (Cádiz) and the Phoenician ports of the south coast run the Atlantic metal trade
Rome's second treaty with Carthage bars Roman ships beyond Mastia in the south-east
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir and begins Carthage's conquest of southern Spain
After the Carthaginian defeat at Ilipa, Gadir makes its own treaty with Rome
Rome organises Nearer and Further Spain as two provinces
Numantia falls; Rome's long Celtiberian wars end

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, the greatest Phoenician city of the west
Hannibal is defeated at Zama; Carthage loses its fleet and its empire
Rome destroys Carthage and makes its land the province of Africa

states.name: Ireland
timeline: Ierne, the 'Sacred Isle' of the Hierni, beyond the tin islands in Himilco's account

states.name: United Kingdom
timeline: Britons stream tin from the granite of Cornwall and Devon
Pytheas describes the tin-workers of Belerion and the island market of Ictis
Italian wine reaches Hengistbury Head through traders from Armorica
Crassus makes the tin route known; whether he reached Britain itself is uncertain

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscans, Italic peoples and Greek cities; Rome is a city-state allied by treaty with Carthage
Tarentum surrenders: Rome controls the Italian peninsula
Carthage loses Sicily to Rome after the First Punic War

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Tin and gold of the north-west, worked by Celtic peoples of the Atlantic coast
The Lusitanians rise against Rome
Decimus Brutus crosses the Douro and the Lima into Gallaecia, the tin country

events.title: Gadir's tin market
events.text: Gadir, founded by Tyre beyond the Pillars of Hercules, is the western Mediterranean's great market for Atlantic tin and silver.

events.title: The Vix krater
events.text: A Celtic princess is buried at Mont Lassois with a huge Greek bronze krater, wealth from the trade routes through Gaul.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Carthage is defeated by the Greeks of Sicily and turns its ambitions west and south.

events.title: Hanno sails south
events.text: According to a Greek translation of his report, the Carthaginian Hanno sails down the Atlantic coast of Africa to found colonies.

events.title: Himilco sails north
events.text: Carthage sends Himilco to explore the outer coasts of Europe; his report survives only in later quotations.

events.title: The Oestrymnides
events.text: Himilco's account tells of islands rich in tin and lead, traded by people in hide boats; their location is debated.

events.title: The Sacred Isle
events.text: Two days' sail beyond the tin islands lies the island of the Hierni, with Albion nearby.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Carthage's second treaty with Rome forbids Roman ships to trade or plunder beyond Mastia in Spain.

events.title: Pytheas sets out
events.text: The Greek explorer Pytheas leaves Massalia for the Atlantic and the far north.

events.title: Uxisama
events.text: Pytheas passes the island of Ushant off Armorica on the way to Britain.

events.title: Belerion
events.text: Pytheas, as quoted by later writers, describes the tin-miners of Britain's south-west tip as hospitable and civilised.

events.title: Ictis
events.text: Tin is carried at low tide to the island of Ictis, where merchants buy it; St Michael's Mount and Mount Batten are candidates.

events.title: Kantion
events.text: Pytheas names Kantion, the south-eastern corner of the island he calls Prettanike.

events.title: Orcades
events.text: Pytheas reports the Orcades at Britain's northern tip; beyond them, six days' sail, lies Thule.

events.title: Mount Batten
events.text: A harbour on Plymouth Sound trades metals across the Channel through the Iron Age.

events.title: Rome rules Italy
events.text: With the surrender of Tarentum, Rome controls the Italian peninsula.

events.title: First Punic War
events.text: Rome and Carthage go to war over Sicily; the war lasts twenty-three years.

events.title: Sicily lost
events.text: Defeated at sea off the Aegates Islands, Carthage gives up Sicily.

events.title: Hamilcar at Gadir
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir to build a new Carthaginian empire in Spain.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal founds Carthago Nova, Carthage's capital in Spain, beside its silver mines.

events.title: Saguntum
events.text: Hannibal besieges and takes Saguntum, Rome's ally, starting the Second Punic War.

events.title: Hannibal crosses the Rhône
events.text: Hannibal's army, with its elephants, crosses the Rhône on its march to Italy.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army at Cannae in southern Italy.

events.title: New Carthage falls
events.text: Scipio captures Carthago Nova in a surprise attack across its lagoon.

events.title: Ilipa
events.text: Scipio defeats the Carthaginians at Ilipa, ending their power in Spain.

events.title: Gades joins Rome
events.text: Gadir, now Gades, surrenders and makes a treaty with Rome.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama; Carthage loses its fleet and overseas empire.

events.title: Two Spains
events.text: Rome creates the provinces of Nearer and Further Spain.

events.title: Lusitanian War
events.text: The Lusitanians of western Iberia rise against Roman rule.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: After a three-year siege, Rome razes Carthage and enslaves its survivors.

events.title: Viriathus killed
events.text: The Lusitanian leader Viriathus is murdered by his own men, bribed by Rome.

events.title: Into Gallaecia
events.text: Decimus Junius Brutus leads a Roman army across the Lima river into the tin country of the north-west.

events.title: Scipio's questions
events.text: Polybius writes that Scipio Aemilianus asked merchants of Massalia, Narbo and Corbilo about Britain; none could tell him anything worth recording.

events.title: Numantia falls
events.text: After a long siege, Scipio takes Numantia; Rome's Celtiberian wars end.

events.title: Transalpine Gaul
events.text: Rome defeats the Allobroges and Arverni and annexes southern Gaul.

events.title: The captain's wreck
events.text: Strabo tells of a Gadir captain who ran his ship aground to stop Romans following him; he gives no date or place.

events.title: Narbo founded
events.text: Rome founds the colony of Narbo Martius on the road from Italy to Spain.

events.title: Arausio
events.text: The migrating Cimbri and Teutones destroy two Roman armies at Arausio.

events.title: Wine at Hengistbury
events.text: Italian wine amphorae reach the harbour of Hengistbury Head, shipped by Gaulish traders from Armorica.

events.title: Crassus finds the route
events.text: Publius Crassus, governor of Further Spain, crosses to the Cassiterides and publishes the route.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries, by who held or reached each one in a given year. Regions are today's boundaries, and whole countries stand for ancient coasts and peoples: Spain counts as Punic for Gadir and its sister ports, though its interior was Iberian and Celtic. A deliberate simplification; many dates, and the location of the Tin Islands, are uncertain.
